neighbours.label: an absolute word that turns a statement into a sweeping, exceptionless claim (all, any, every, must, certainly, always)
fire: Every reasonable person certainly agrees that children deserve clean water.
Any serious historian must admit that the records are biased.
All human beings, without exception, need sleep to stay healthy.
Whatever the critics say, the plan will always fail in the end.
Everyone obviously knows that fire is hot.
No matter how hard you try, you can never please every customer.
Every single cell in the body certainly depends on oxygen.
Anyone who reads the report must conclude that the bridge is unsafe.
quiet: Some reasonable people think that children may need more water.
A few historians have suggested that the records might be biased.
Many human beings seem to need around eight hours of sleep.
According to some critics, the plan could run into trouble.
Several people mentioned that the stove felt warm.
If you try hard, you may be able to please some customers.
Some cells in the body can survive briefly without oxygen.
People who read the report might wonder whether the bridge is safe.

predictions: Sweeping universal or certainty claims fire weakly (around 0.2-0.4); hedged versions of the same claims stay below 0.1.
notes: Card top: must, greatest, certainly, all, obviously, wholly, only, no matter. Probe: 'must admit' 0.27, 'every living thing' 0.21, 'no matter where... always' 0.23, 'everyone certainly knows' 0.41; hedged 'some/may/a few' 0.05-0.085. Effects are small, so the median may miss 0.20.
